starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: Aghhh get that cat away from me. Quickly please.

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.player: Why? What's your problem with it?

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: Just take it away please. Take it away. If you do, I'll tell you of the secret passageway.

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: Get the cat away from me first and then I'll tell you.

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.player: Okay, now where is this passage?

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: It's by that group of rocks just to the north east, but you won't be able to enter. Well, not yet anyway...

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: To Sophanem, the city of the dead.

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: The second city of the Menaphites, full of giant monuments to their departed.

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: The place is locked down at the moment, so the passage is the only way in. Apparently, they've been hit by a set of plagues. That pathetic new High Priest of Icthlarin is probably to blame.

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.player: Interesting... Tell me about this Icthlarin.
So why do you say I won't be able to enter the passage?

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: First bring me some supplies and then I'll tell you. I'm running low and I'm about to embark on a long journey.

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.speaker: Wanderer
starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.text: Get me a full waterskin and a tinderbox. I seem to have lost my own and these desert nights are very cold.

starting-out-meeting-the-wanderer.prompt: Start the Icthlarin's Little Helper quest?

steps.text: If the player already has a full waterskin and a tinderbox:

steps.player: Okay. I actually have those on me already.

steps.text: If the player does not:

steps.player: Okay, I'll get you your supplies.
Sorry, I've got other things to do.

steps.speaker: Wanderer
steps.text: Fool! Only I can give you the knowledge on the secret passageway!

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Hiss

steps.speaker: Wanderer
steps.text: Get that cat away from me!

steps.player: Yes. I have them here.

steps.text: Bring me a full waterskin and a tinderbox.

starting-out-entering-the-wanderer-s-ten.player: Yuck! It smells like there's dead cats in there or something. I'm not going in.

city-of-the-dead.text: You slowly pick yourself off the ground. Your head is pounding, and an irrational sense of guilt nags you.

city-of-the-dead.player: Ah, my poor head. What's going on?
How did I get here? That wanderer... This is her doing!

city-of-the-dead.text: You notice a ghostly figure making pained gestures in your direction.
If a ghostspeak amulet is worn:

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: You foul thief, return what is mine!

steps.player: What?

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: You heard me! Restore what you have stolen from my tomb!

steps.player: But...

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: Wooo wooo wooooo!
The spirit tries to converse with you, but all you can understand is his anger, which is directed toward you.

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: Spawn of evil!

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: Organ snatcher!

steps.speaker: Klenter

steps.speaker: Klenter

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: Grave defiler!

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: You pathetic excuse for a thief!

steps.speaker: Klenter

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: Grave robber!

steps.speaker: Klenter
steps.text: Wooo wooo wooooo!
The spirit tries to converse with you, but all you can understand is his anger, which is directed toward you.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-jex.speaker: Jex

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-jex-attempti.speaker: Jex

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-raetul.speaker: Raetul

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-siamun.speaker: Siamun

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-carpente.speaker: Carpenter
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-carpente.text: Get away from me you filthy grave robber.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-embalmer.speaker: Embalmer
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-embalmer.text: Clear off you evil body snatcher! You won't get any of my wares.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-tal.speaker: Priest
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-tal.text: What business do you have with a servant of Icthlarin?

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-tal.player: I need some help figuring out what's going on.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-tal.speaker: Priest
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-tal.text: I will not aid a defiler of the dead. Be gone!

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-tal.player: Hello. Can I go through this gate?

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-tal.speaker: Priest
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-tal.text: No. Nobody may enter or leave Sophanem for any reason due to the quarantine. Move along.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-att.speaker: Priest
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-a-priest-att.text: Sorry, but Sophanem is under quarantine. No one may leave or enter.

steps.player: But I'm not infected with anything!

steps.speaker: Priest
steps.text: I'm afraid my orders are clear.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-high-pri.speaker: High Priest
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-high-pri.text: You! I will have no dealings with those who plunder the houses of the dead.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-high-pri.speaker: High Priest
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-high-pri.text: Get thee gone from my presence!

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.text: If the player has a cat follower or in the inventory:

steps.player: Good day.

steps.text: The Sphinx ignores you.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Ah, how interesting... a cat. Come here to me, kitty.

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Meow.
Your cat and the Sphinx converse in a yeowling language for a short time.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.speaker: Sphinx
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.text: Yes, your companion tells me that you are in a spot of bother.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.player: What companion? Oh, you mean my pet cat?
Do you have any idea what happened to me? One moment I was talking to a wanderer in the desert, the next I was here. I also have a cracking headache.
Yes. She had red hair, and weird red eyes as well.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.speaker: Sphinx
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.text: Interesting, very interesting. I'm afraid I do not know what happened to you, but it sounds like quite a bit occurred between you meeting that wanderer and now.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.player: But I can't remember any of it.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.speaker: Sphinx
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx.text: Then I suggest you find something to remind you. I find that important objects and locations can trigger memories, no matter how repressed they are.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx-t.speaker: Sphinx
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx-t.text: We've already had this conversation, have we not? You're in a spot of bother, but you can't remember what happened to you.

city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx-t.speaker: Sphinx
city-of-the-dead-talking-to-the-sphinx-t.text: Perhaps you should try to find something to remind you again. I find that important objects and locations can trigger memories, no matter how repressed they are.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: As you touch the pyramid door, a sense of deja-vu sweeps over you...
The player has a flashback of inside the pyramid
(The canopic jar is replaced with an unholy symbol)

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: I must go to the heart of the pyramid... The mistress commands it...
I must get to the heard of the pyramid...

steps.text: The flashback ends early

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: I remember! That wanderer, she hypnotised me!
But... I can't remember why. I needed to get... something. This is so confusing...
Maybe someone around here can tell me what on Gielinor is going on.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Well, you should have thought of that before you risked it for some advice from a crazy old Sphinx.

steps.player: Could you at least help me now?

steps.speaker: Sphinx

options.text: I don't know. I don't want to risk my cat.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Too true, you didn't rob just anybody's grave. You managed to rob the grave of Klenter, the recently deceased High Priest of Icthlarin. Do you know what that means?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Icthlarin is the Menaphite god of the dead. By desecrating the tomb of one of his priests, you've made an enemy out of every person in this city.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: But I didn't desecrate any tomb! There's no proof!

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Really? Because if I'm not mistaken, that's Klenter's shade right over there. He definitely doesn't seem happy with you. There's also the burial jar in your possession. How do you explain that?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: How did you know about the burial jar?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: I can smell the rotting organs from here.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: Look, I don't know exactly what happened. All I know is that wanderer hypnotised me and had me steal something from this pyramid.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: The burial jar?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: I... I guess so. It's all still very unclear.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Interesting. I'm afraid I can't help you. I have my own concerns without involving myself with petty human affairs.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: However, I suggest you seek out the new High Priest of Icthlarin to the south east. He might be able to assist you. Of course, you'll need to convince him to talk to you first.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Sphinx
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: Here, I have a token that he will know is from me. Take that to him, and I'm sure he will speak with you.
The Sphinx gives you a token.

options.text: What's going on in this city?
I'll go speak with the High Priest.

steps.player: I'll go speak with the High Priest.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: If the player does not have a cat follower or in the inventory:

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: I have no interest in speaking with you. You should bring your cat to me again. The two of us have much to discuss.
If the Sphinx previously stole the player's cat:

steps.player: But you stole my last one!

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Well, you would be well advised to get another.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: If the player has a cat follower or in the inventory:

steps.text: The Sphinx ignores you.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Ah, how interesting... a cat. Come here to me, kitty.

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Meow.
Your cat and the Sphinx converse in a yeowling language for a short time.

steps.player: I lost that token you gave me. Could I have another please?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Ah, you humans.
The Sphinx gives you another token.

steps.player: Thanks.
Tell me about yourself.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: I am an agent of neither good nor evil. I am unconcerned with the plight of mankind and their petty wars and beliefs.

steps.player: Well, now that you've told me what you're not, can you perhaps tell me what you are?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: I am the guardian of feline kind.

steps.player: Why would they need a guardian?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Cats play a significant role in the religion of this area, particularly when it comes to guarding the dead from the Devourer.

steps.player: The Devourer?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: She's the very incarnation of destruction.

steps.player: I don't understand.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: What understanding do you have of the Menaphite gods?

steps.player: Little to none.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Well the Menaphite Pantheon is made up of four main deities.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: The two main gods of the pantheon are Tumeken, the god of light, and Elidinis, the goddess of fertility.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Tumeken and Elidinis also have two children. Icthlarin is one, and the Devourer is the other.

steps.player: They named her the Devourer? Not great at parenting, were they?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: She was not always called such. She is known by her deeds now, rather than her name.

steps.player: So if the Devourer is the bad sibling, does that make Icthlarin the good one?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: That is the common belief, but things are rarely that simple. In some ways, neither of them are good or bad.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Icthlarin is the god of the dead. He takes care of the passing of souls to their next life. The Devourer is the goddess of destruction, and that is what she craves.

steps.player: I thought you said she wasn't evil?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: That's not quite what I said. Still, is destruction enough to make one evil? Fire destroys, but is that evil?

steps.player: Um... no, but it also creates heat.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: We could have an overlong theological debate now, but let's instead get to my point. Destruction has a place, so maybe the Devourer does as well. However, she has taken it too far.

steps.player: How?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: The Devourer wishes to destroy every soul in existence, living or dead. As you can imagine, this has brought her into conflict with Icthlarin.

steps.player: Ah, I see where this is going. The cats are used to protect the dead from the Devourer, like you said earlier. But who protects the cats?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Well anticipated. The Devourer is terrified of cats for reasons I will not explain. However, her followers, although few in number, are not. I ensure the survival of cats. For this service, Icthlarin grants me eternal life.

steps.player: So, then, you are a follower of Icthlarin?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Nothing of the sort. As I've said before, I have no interest in humans and their gods. I look after my kind. For that, Icthlarin looks after me.

options.text: What's going on in this city?
This is all very interesting, but I've got to get going.

steps.player: This is all very interesting, but I've got to get going.

options.text: What's going on in this city?

steps.player: What's going on in this city?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: I thought that would be pretty obvious.

steps.player: Well, I could benefit from your point of view. You seem the independent type.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Flattery, my adventurer, will get you everywhere. But to answer your question, Sophanem has been struck with plagues.

steps.player: More than one?

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Quite a number. There's a plague of frogs to the west. In the east, you can also find locusts.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: The cows have only been producing sour milk since the outbreak, and the residents have been struck down by a rash of spots.

steps.player: The residents? There are a lot of living people here for a city of the dead.

steps.speaker: Sphinx
steps.text: Sophanem is called the city of the dead because the dead are brought here. Death plays a rather large role in the beliefs of the people and, as a result, the business.

options.text: This is all very interesting, but I've got to get going.

steps.player: This is all very interesting, but I've got to get going.

options.text: I'll go speak with the High Priest.

steps.player: I'll go speak with the High Priest.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Priest
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: What do you want, cursed one?

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: The Sphinx told me to find the High Priest of Icthlarin.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: Priest
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: A likely story. She would never reduce herself to talk to one as lowly as you, never mind help you!

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: High Priest
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: You! I will have no dealings with those who plunder the houses of the dead.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.player: Wait! The Sphinx told me that I should talk to you.

figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.speaker: High Priest
figuring-out-what-on-gielinor-is-going-o.text: The Sphinx? Is it possible? That contrary old cat has never done anything to help us. Prove it!
If player does not have the token:

steps.player: She gave me a token to show you, but I lost it.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well then stop wasting my time! Can't you see I'm trying to put a stop to these plagues?
If the player has the token:
You hand the token to the High Priest.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well this is... unexpected...

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: So what do you want from me, thief?

steps.player: I appreciate it doesn't look great right now, but I'm not actually a bad person.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well you could have fooled me! Good people don't rob from the dead!

steps.player: It wasn't me! Well... it was, I guess. I didn't do it on purpose though. I was hypnotised!

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Hypnotised?

steps.player: Yes! There was this wanderer! She had me break into that pyramid to steal... a burial jar... I think. It's all still a bit confusing.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: This is all a disaster! The plagues were bad enough, but now we've got hypnotised adventurers plundering tombs! I've only just started this job as well!

steps.player: You do seem to be going through a rough patch. Do you know what caused the plagues?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: We fear they are a punishment sent by the gods. Perhaps we have displeased Icthlarin in some way. Maybe I am to blame. All this only started after I became High Priest.

steps.player: Well I'm not sure if I can help with your plagues, but I need to fix whatever mess I caused in that pyramid. Can you help me?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Oh, er... I suppose the burial jar you took must be returned as soon as possible. That will allow my predecessor to rest once more.

steps.player: I can do that. Do you have any advice for me when it comes to the pyramid?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I don't think so... No wait! There is something important.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: As with many of our tombs, the pyramid has magical seals to protect it from the Devourer, the goddess of destruction. The fact that you were able to get in before means that you must have a cat.

steps.player: Well... yes. But how did you know that?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Cats act as guardians against the Devourer. I'm surprised the Sphinx didn't tell you this. As such, only a cat can open the pyramid door.

steps.player: I see. I guess that makes sense.

options.text: Why is it so important that the jar be returned?
Can you tell me more about the plagues.
Can you tell me more about Icthlarin.
Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

putting-things-right-talking-to-the-high.text: If the player does not have the canopic jar:

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: One of my priests found this lying outside the pyramid. Please try to be more respectful of our dead.
The High Priest gives you a burial jar.

steps.player: Oops. I'll make sure I look after it this time. Sorry.

putting-things-right-talking-to-the-high.text: If the player has the jar:

steps.player: Hello.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Have you managed to return the jar yet?

steps.player: No, not yet.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Please hurry. The people are beginning to... well...

steps.player: What? Question your sanity?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: No, just my authority. Don't forget that to enter the pyramid, you'll need a cat.

options.text: Why is it so important that the jar be returned?

steps.player: Why is it so important that the jar be returned?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well those jars are a key part of our burial practices. To remove one is to directly insult not just Icthlarin, but all those that have passed on to the next life.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Not to mention, it wasn't just any jar you took. You stole a jar from the tomb of our former High Priest! Why do you think his ghost is now wandering the city once more?

steps.player: But what will happen if I don't return the jar?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Have you not noticed the plagues already filling our city? How long before Klenter calls upon Icthlarin to send a few more?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: For all we know, the plagues we already have could be punishment for your grave robbing!

steps.player: Hey, don't go blaming me for that. Those plagues were here before I even met that wanderer!

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Perhaps Icthlarin foresaw what would happen and sent the plagues as a pre-emptive punishment?

steps.player: You really think he'd do that?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I don't know... Icthlarin is a patient and forgiving god. It does not make sense to me that he would do this to us.

steps.player: Maybe he's not the one responsible.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Perhaps. Either way, that jar needs to be returned.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the plagues.

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the plagues.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: They started a few days ago. We have locusts in the east of the city and frogs in the west. The cows have started to produce sour milk, and all of us have become infected with some sort of pox.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Once it became clear how bad it was, Menaphos, our neighbouring city, closed their gates to us and everyone else. We closed our own gates soon after.

steps.player: That can't have been an easy choice to make.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: I didn't want to, but the other priests insisted. We had to stop the plagues from spreading. It seems that our choice was the right one. So far, the plagues have remained contained, but at a great cost.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Many of our citizens are trapped outside the city. Some are stuck in Menaphos, with more in other parts of the desert.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: However, that may well be for the best. Without trade from other settlements, we've been struggling to even feed the few of us left in the city.

steps.player: How much longer do you think you can last?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Not long. We need to find a way to stop the plagues soon.

options.text: Can you tell me more about Icthlarin.

steps.player: Can you tell me more about Icthlarin.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Icthlarin is the son of Tumeken and Elidinis and brother to the Devourer. He is the Menaphite god of the dead. He is responsible for ensuring the safe passage of all souls from this life to the next.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Here in Sophanem, we support Icthlarin in his role by making sure the dead are suitably prepared for their journey.

steps.player: So is Icthlarin only responsible for those that die in the desert?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: No. While Icthlarin is only worshipped here, his responsibilities stretch across all of Gielinor. He cares not for an individual's beliefs. All who pass on, enter his care.

steps.player: I imagine there are plenty of people out there who have a different take on things.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Which they are welcome to. It does not change the facts.

steps.player: You seem very sure in these 'facts'.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: While most of the gods, Tumeken and Elidinis included, may be long gone from Gielinor, Icthlarin remains. His important role in caring for the dead means that he is still able to interact with us.

steps.player: So you've met him?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Well... no. While he is able to walk among us if he desires, he chooses not to so as to respect our way of life. Not to mention, his role requires his constant attention.

steps.player: I see. Fair enough.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

steps.player: Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Long ago, back when Tumeken and Elidinis still walked these lands, they had two children. Icthlarin, god of the dead, was one. The other was Amascut, the goddess of rebirth.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: For a time, Icthlarin and Amascut worked together in harmony. Icthlarin would ensure most souls are safely guided to the next life, while Amascut would select a small number to be reborn.

steps.player: But something happened?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Yes. During a great war over these lands, Amascut became corrupted. She was warped into the Devourer, becoming the goddess of destruction.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Since then, her only goal has been to devour every soul in existence, both living and dead.

steps.player: The Sphinx told me something similar, but her interpretation was a bit different.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: We here have a lot of respect for the Sphinx. However, you should be careful of her words. She does not know the gods like we priests do.

steps.player: So is the Devourer still around?

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Unfortunately so. Most gods have long since left this world. However, the Devourer was able to find a way to remain.

steps.speaker: High Priest
steps.text: Luckily for us, some of her former priestesses were able to weaken her, but she still poses a great threat.

steps.player: I'd better get going.

putting-things-right-talking-to-a-priest.speaker: Priest
putting-things-right-talking-to-a-priest.text: Cursed one, why have you not yet returned the burial jar of our old leader?

putting-things-right-talking-to-a-priest.speaker: Priest
putting-things-right-talking-to-a-priest.text: I wonder how someone as insignificant as you even managed to get inside the pyramid, never mind reach its heart.

putting-things-right-talking-to-jex-afte.speaker: Jex
putting-things-right-talking-to-jex-afte.text: Hello there. Welcome to the Temple of the Lesser Gods.

options.text: Could you tell me more about the lesser gods?

steps.text: (Continues in Transcript:Jex)

steps.player: I'd better get going.

steps.player: Fine. Come on, cat. Lets leave the nasty Sphinx alone.

steps.speaker: Cat

putting-things-right-flashback-2-jumping.player: I need to get the burial jar for the mistress...

putting-things-right-flashback-2-jumping.speaker: Apparition
putting-things-right-flashback-2-jumping.text: You will not defile this place!

putting-things-right-flashback-2-jumping.player: So I really did steal the jar. I need to return it as fast as I can.

putting-things-right-attempting-to-take-.player: I've already caused enough trouble over these jars. I'll just leave them alone.

putting-things-right-talking-to-a-priest.speaker: Priest
putting-things-right-talking-to-a-priest.text: Bother me not. I am preparing for the ceremony. I'm sure even you can curb your trivial demands until after that.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Have you managed to return the jar yet?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Wonderful! Now we can prepare for the ceremony.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: The ceremony to reconsecrate Klenter's tomb of course!

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: It would have been nice for you to mention this earlier.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Sorry, with all this plague business, it must have slipped my mind.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: You're the High Priest of Icthlarin, but you forgot a key ceremony?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Well if you want to try running a city with multiple plagues, you're welcome to take over.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: That's not what I... Never mind.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Good. Now, this ceremony is very dangerous, so we must ensure everything is done correctly.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Well the pyramid has these magical seals on it...

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: ... to protect it from the Devourer. Yes, you told me earlier.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Right! Of course I did. Well for us to properly reconsecrate the tomb, we must first remove those seals. That means that once we begin, the pyramid will be vulnerable until the ceremony is complete.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Now, we made many of the preparations while you were gone, but the carpenter and the embalmer could both use a hand. Could you go and speak with them?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: Why do I have to help?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Did you forget that this is all your fault?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: I guess I assumed that by returning the jar I stole, my job would be done.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: The job will be done when Klenter is at rest once more.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: Besides, thanks to the plagues, we're not allowing people to leave the city. However, as you seem to be unaffected, I've told the guards to make an exception for you.

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.player: And that means I'm best placed to help. Fine. The carpenter and the embalmer, did you say?

putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.speaker: High Priest
putting-things-right-informing-the-high-.text: That's right. We need the carpenter to create a new holy symbol for the ceremony. He lives over to the east. The embalmer also needs help gathering some supplies. He lives just south of here.

options.text: Can you tell me more about the plagues.

Can you tell me more about the Devourer.

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
ceremony-preparations-talking-to-the-hig.text: The embalmer lives just south of here and the carpenter lives over to the east. Please hurry. We need to get this ceremony performed before some other bad thing happens.

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-a-pries.player: Hello. Can I go through this gate?

ceremony-preparations-talking-to-a-pries.speaker: Priest
ceremony-preparations-talking-to-a-pries.text: Yes. The High Priest has given you permission to come and go as you please.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Oh, it's you. I hear you're helping us now. To be honest, I'm still not thrilled to have you around, but so be it.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.player: I guess that's probably the best I can ask for, given the situation. Anyway, the High Priest said you needed help gathering some supplies for the ceremony.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: That's right. I need three things, but the quarantine is making some of them hard to obtain.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: First, I need some salt. Normally I get mine from the salt lake just north of the city. Just fill a bucket from the lake and then use the suntrap outside to separate the salt from the water.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Next, I need some tree sap. You can use a knife to extract some from a tree, but make sure you have a bucket ready. Most coniferous evergreen trees should have some. They're the cone-shaped ones.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.speaker: Embalmer
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: Finally, I need some linen. That one shouldn't be too hard. The local cloth salesman should have some.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has salt:

steps.text: You hand some salt to the embalmer.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has linen:

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player gave an item to the Embalmer:

steps.speaker: Embalmer
steps.text: Well that was unexpected. Thank you.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: You cut the tree and allow some sap to drip into your bucket.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: If the player has a bucket of saltwater:

pile of salt

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.text: It's hot and sunny, which is good enough for me. So can I help you with anything?

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-embalme.player: I've met with the town's embalmer and he mentioned that he needed a few things, linen being one of them.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.player: That's right. He asked me to come and speak to you about a holy symbol for the ceremony.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Ah yes, it needs to be made from willow. Thing is, there's a small problem with that.

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.player: Is this the part where you need me to get you something?

ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.speaker: Carpenter
ceremony-preparations-aiding-the-carpent.text: Wow, you're quick. I'm all out of willow, and due to the quarantine, I'm unable to leave the city to get more. However, the High Priest mentioned that a special exception has been made for you.

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.speaker: Amascut
the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: You! Priest of the dog lord. You are now mine. Kill your brethren!

the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-opening-the-door-t.text: Protect us, adventurer! We must complete the ceremony!

the-devourer-revealed-defeating-the-pose.text: The priest seems to recover from the Devourer's spell

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-a-pries.speaker: Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-a-pries.text: You have surprised me... I commend you for your efforts.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: Thank you so much, adventurer. Thanks to you, we were able to complete the ceremony.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.player: Well it was the least I could do. After all, it was sort of my fault all this happened.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: Well on that note, what exactly did happen there? That was the Devourer!

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.player: It seems the wanderer that hypnotised me was actually the Devourer all along.
I'm guessing the reason she had me steal that burial jar was because she knew you'd have to gather here to reconsecrate the tomb again.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: She wanted to kill us all in one go?

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.player: Yes, and she had me plant an unholy symbol here to allow her to teleport right in.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: Well once again, thank you. Without you, the Devourer would have struck a devastating blow against Icthlarin.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.player: Here's that holy symbol, by the way.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: You give the holy symbol to the High Priest.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: Thank you. We wouldn't have been able to complete the ceremony without that in our presence.

the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.speaker: High Priest
the-devourer-revealed-talking-to-the-hig.text: We have a few things to finish here, but then we'll head back up into the city. Please join us there.

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.text: All of a sudden, a final sense of deja-vu sweeps over you...
The player has a flashback of meeting Icthlarin in the pyramid

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.speaker: Icthlarin
the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.text: And what do we have here?

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.player: I must do as the mistress commands...

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.speaker: Icthlarin
the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.text: Did my sister really think that I would not sense her presence here?

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.speaker: Icthlarin
the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.text: Amascut! Release your hold on this human!

the-devourer-revealed-flashback-4-leavin.player: Well I guess that explains why Amascut's control over me was broken. Not every day the god of the dead comes to your rescue.

finishing-up-speaking-with-the-high-prie.speaker: High Priest
finishing-up-speaking-with-the-high-prie.text: Ah, there you are. You were gone for quite a while. As a thank you for what you've done, I have a little trinket for you. I'm sure you'll get a huge amount of enjoyment out of it.

finishing-up-trying-to-enter-the-pyramid.player: I think it would be best if I stayed out of this tomb after what happened last time.

trpgum.speaker: Sphinx
trpgum.text: I have no interest in speaking with you. You should bring your cat to me again. The two of us have much to discuss.

46UaUb.player: I think the High Priest mentioned something about needing a cat to enter the pyramid.
